title: Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yuchasin cites that he was R-H’s student, and Seder HaDorot wrote “I have not found it.” Hyman finds support in [Pesachim 106b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.106b.2) (106a in Hyman’s citation), where he reports a Dikdukei Soferim reading in which Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina asks Rav Huna whether someone who tasted food may recite havdalah. Hyman’s received reading is Rav Chana bar Chinena.[^6] In [Yevamot 79a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.79a.4-5) he raises an objection to R-H’s words. In Yoma 54b in Hyman’s citation (compare [Yoma 54a:11-14](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.54a.11-14)): “Rav Ketina said — Rav Chisda objected — Rav Nachman said — Rav Chisda objected — Rav Nachman said — Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina objected — he said to him: Do you say ‘she was divorced’?” etc. — and this refers to Rav Nachman, or he objects to Rav Ketina his father.

He is mentioned in [Taanit 13a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13a.6), [Kiddushin 77b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.77b.8) and [Bekhorot 37b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.37b.14). Hyman refers to an objection to Rabbah in [Nedarim 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.65b.3) and gives the name R-H son of Rav Ketina.[^6] He reports that the Rosh’s Piskei reads Rav Chana. Likewise in [Chullin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.17b.13), R-H son of Rav Ketina transmits a teaching in the name of Resh Lakish; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chana. In Zevachim 115a [1] in Hyman’s citation (compare [Zevachim 115b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.115b.6)), Hyman quotes “R-H bar R-Q sat before Rav Chisda.” He reports “Rav Chana bar R-Q” as the reading of Shitah Mekubbetzet and the Bach.[^7] In [Chullin 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.19a.2-3): “Rav Chanan son of Rav Ketina said to R-N: According to whom? — He said to him: I know neither chilak nor bilak,” etc.; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chana.

The recovered Wikisource footnote corrects the citation to Zevachim 115b. The consulted text there gives Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina. Hyman prints 115a and attributes the reading Rav Chana to Shitah Mekubbetzet and the Bach. His printed notice reads והב״ח, whereas the supplied transcription reads ורב״ח.

The quoted exchange is on Yoma 54a in the consulted edition. The printed Hyman notice cites 54b and gives one objection by Rav Chisda and one reply by Rav Nachman, as in the consulted passage. The supplied transcription repeats both. Hyman leaves open whether Rav Chana objects to Rav Nachman or to his father Rav Ketina.

The consulted Rosh on Nedarim names Rav Chana bar Rav Ketina and Rabbah. The consulted Bavli at Nedarim 65b instead names Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina speaking to the rabbis. Chullin 19a has Rav Chanan addressing Rav Nachman, alongside the variant Chana reported by Hyman.

[Seder HaDorot 1377](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1377&lang=en) says the notice identifying this sage as Rav Huna’s student had eluded him. [Pesachim 106b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.106b.2) names Rav Chana bar Chinena as the questioner. Hyman reports Rav Chana son of Rav Ketina from Dikdukei Soferim. [Yevamot 79a:4–5](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.79a.4-5) has Rav Chana bar Ketina, [Chullin 17b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.17b.13) has Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina, and [Chullin 19a:2–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.19a.2-3) has Rav Chanan bar Rav Ketina. The linked [Nedarim 65b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.65b.3) has Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina address the rabbis. Hyman names Rabbah as the addressee.

The consulted Yoma passage has one objection by Rav Chisda and one reply by Rav Nachman before Rav Chana objects. The consulted Zevachim passage has Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina reading before Rav Chisda. Hyman reports Rav Chana as a variant.
